anchor: Three results follow. First, calibrated per-request timing exposes language-pool latency tails that the simulator's default polynomial flattens. Second, the vision pool's cost model admits an exact batching law, grounding a realistic cross-request batching policy and an analytic bound on the inter-pool handoff. Third, and centrally, arrival-speedup sweeps locate each pool's saturation knee: on steady traffic the knees sit an order of magnitude apart.
claim_text: Three main results: (1) calibrated timing reveals language-pool latency tails hidden by polynomial model; (2) vision pool cost model yields exact batching law and analytic handoff bound; (3) arrival-speedup sweeps show saturation knees an order of magnitude apart on steady traffic.

anchor: Inside the trace's largest burst both pools violate the evaluation SLA at the locked naive topology in structurally different ways: a removable language-pool prefill floor against episodic vision-pool queueing invisible to rate- and utilization-based monitoring.
claim_text: In the largest burst, both pools violate SLA at naive topology: language pool has removable prefill floor, vision pool has episodic queueing invisible to rate/utilization monitors.

anchor: Dynamo's discrete-event worker simulator (the mocker) models text token processing only, so the vision stage cannot live inside it. The composition instead runs the vision pool as an event-driven FIFO of C encoder workers inside the workload converter, costed per forward by AIC's encoder graph on the collected rtx_5090 data, and hands the language pool to dynamo.replay.
claim_text: Simulation architecture: vision pool as event-driven FIFO of C encoder workers costed via AIC encoder graph on RTX 5090 data; language pool handled by dynamo.replay.

anchor: The seam is the trace itself: for an open-loop request, d milliseconds spent in the vision pool equals arriving at the language pool d milliseconds later, so the converter folds each request's encoder delay (queue wait + service + handoff transfer) into its emitted arrival timestamp.
claim_text: Trace seam: vision pool encoder delay (queue wait + service + handoff) folded into language pool arrival timestamps.

anchor: A --no-encoder-shift mode emits raw arrivals instead (the language pool in isolation), enabling the per-pool attribution in the load sweeps below.
claim_text: --no-encoder-shift mode emits raw arrivals for language pool isolation, enabling per-pool attribution in load sweeps.

anchor: The language pool runs offline with a KV-aware router across two simulated workers; per-request prefill and decode times come either from the mocker's default polynomial or from AIC's calibrated h100_sxm/vLLM 0.22.0 database (the locked decoder-pool platform), selected per run.
claim_text: Language pool uses KV-aware router across 2 simulated workers; prefill/decode times from mocker polynomial or AIC calibrated h100_sxm/vLLM 0.22.0 database.

anchor: The entire pipeline is CPU-only and deterministic given a trace window.
claim_text: Pipeline is CPU-only and deterministic for a given trace window.

anchor: The calibrated model is moderately slower on averages and markedly heavier in the tails: TTFT p99 grows 1.24× and the maximum TTFT and inter-token latency roughly double (1.8× and 1.9×).
claim_text: Calibrated model vs polynomial: TTFT p99 1.24× higher, max TTFT 1.8× higher, max inter-token latency 1.9× higher.
Polynomial vs AIC h100: TTFT avg 67.3 vs 68.2 ms, p99 248 vs 307 ms, max 2540 vs 4518 ms.

anchor: Request latency avg / p99 (ms) & 1,413 / 6,879 & 1,590 / 8,163
claim_text: Polynomial vs AIC h100: request latency avg 1413 vs 1590 ms, p99 6879 vs 8163 ms.

anchor: Inter-token latency avg / max (ms) & 6.79 / 181 & 7.67 / 348
claim_text: Polynomial vs AIC h100: inter-token latency avg 6.79 vs 7.67 ms, max 181 vs 348 ms.

anchor: Output tok/s per user (avg) & 160.6 & 142.0
claim_text: Polynomial vs AIC h100: output tokens per user avg 160.6 vs 142.0.

anchor: A spot-check prices the family flagship, Qwen3-VL-235B-A22B at TP8, on the same shipped H100 data, window, and topology: ~2× the 8B's decode latency throughout, with ITL p99 already 87.7 ms at the trace's own rate, so the decode bound moves and its knee drops to s=1 against the 8B's s=2 --- decoder scale halves the language pool's operating envelope.
claim_text: Qwen3-VL-235B-A22B at TP8: ~2× decode latency of 8B, ITL p99 87.7 ms at trace rate, knee drops to s=1 vs 8B's s=2, halving operating envelope.

anchor: The vision side needs no such caveat: the ViT and its 4096-dimensional projector output are identical between the 8B and the 235B, so the encoder cost model, batching law, burst-saturation result, and handoff bound all transfer to the flagship unchanged.
claim_text: Vision encoder cost model, batching law, burst-saturation result, handoff bound identical between 8B and 235B models.

anchor: AIC's encoder graph prices a forward exactly by its total images: every factoring of N images into (batch, images-per-request) --- (1,64) or (64,1) --- returns the same latency to the microsecond, because attention is evaluated at the product batch×images and every other operator at the total token count.
claim_text: Encoder graph latency depends only on total images, not batch/images-per-request factoring; latency identical to microsecond.

anchor: Each dispatched batch is therefore costed at its image total, and batching pays: f(1) = 8.16 ms per image alone versus f(64) = 316.4 ms: 4.94 ms per image amortized, a 1.65× throughput gain.
claim_text: Batching gain: f(1)=8.16 ms/image, f(64)=316.4 ms total (4.94 ms/image), 1.65× throughput gain.

anchor: (Measured end-to-end the realized gain is smaller and saturates by N≈6--8 on both execution stacks --- conservative for the saturation results below; Section 4.2.)
claim_text: Measured end-to-end batching gain smaller, saturates at N≈6-8 on both execution stacks.

anchor: Dispatch is greedy FIFO: a freed worker takes whole queued requests, in order, up to a 64-image cap (the collected batch range, so no extrapolation); a request exceeding the cap alone (the trace reaches 97^2 = 9409 images) is chunked into ≤64-image forwards that enter the FIFO as independent units, so several free workers drain one oversized request concurrently.
claim_text: Greedy FIFO dispatch with 64-image cap; oversized requests (up to 9409 images) chunked into ≤64-image units processed concurrently.

anchor: Chunk-parallel dispatch is a simulator policy assumption: consistent with encoder-disaggregated runtimes that route image groups independently across encoder instances, physically grounded (images are independent in the encoder), but not a property of the trace.
claim_text: Chunk-parallel dispatch is a simulator policy assumption, not a trace property.

anchor: Under low load the policy changes nothing (steady-head percentiles identical to three decimals); it matters inside bursts.
claim_text: Chunk-parallel policy does not affect steady-head percentiles (identical to three decimals), only matters in bursts.

anchor: The runs charge the main projector stream (post-merge vision embeddings of 196 × 4096 bf16 values per image, ≈1.6 MB per image), bounded analytically as RTT + bytes/bandwidth on a parameterized link (default 25 Gbps): 0.71 ms at the median request of the steady window, 62 ms at its 121-image maximum.
claim_text: Handoff bound: main projector stream 196×4096 bf16 per image (~1.6 MB/image), RTT + bytes/bandwidth at 25 Gbps: 0.71 ms median, 62 ms at 121-image max.

anchor: First, a disaggregated Qwen3-VL deployment must also ship the three DeepStack projections the language model consumes in its early layers (three more such tensors per image), quadrupling the payload to ≈6.4 MB per image (≈250 ms at the 121-image maximum on the default link).
claim_text: DeepStack projections quadruple payload to ~6.4 MB/image (~250 ms at 121-image max on 25 Gbps link).

anchor: Second, the bound is bandwidth-only: contention, serialization points, NIC/PCIe placement, and cross-node topology are not modeled, so it is a lower bound on transfer latency, not a tail estimate; it is charged to request latency but not to the worker (asynchronous DMA/NIC), optimistic for encoder throughput, and a measured NIXL curve can later replace it.
claim_text: Handoff bound is bandwidth-only lower bound, not a tail estimate; charged to request latency not worker; optimistic for encoder throughput.

anchor: The trace records no image sizes, so the uniform 448^2 assumption of Chapter 4 stands, and the cost model matches vLLM's own vision tower within 12.8% across the serving regime.
claim_text: Uniform 448^2 image assumption used; cost model matches vLLM vision tower within 12.8% across serving regime.

anchor: The language pool must hold TTFT p99 < 1 second and inter-token latency (ITL) p99 < 100 ms; the vision pool must hold encoder delay p99 < 1 second, matching the language TTFT budget.
claim_text: Evaluation SLA: language pool TTFT p99 < 1s, ITL p99 < 100ms; vision pool encoder delay p99 < 1s.

anchor: This encoder percentile is taken over all requests --- a text-only request incurs zero encoder delay, so it is a user-population tail, not a vision-pool-conditional one; the stage-conditional (image-bearing) variant is reported alongside it where the distinction matters.
claim_text: Encoder delay p99 computed over all requests (including text-only with zero delay), not conditional on image-bearing requests.

anchor: Summing the two stage budgets gives ≈2 seconds to first token at roughly the p98 level (a union bound over two p99s, not an end-to-end p99 guarantee); a modelled reconstruction on the composed run puts the ingress-to-first-token p99 at ≈1.3 seconds, which the measured request-linked join of Chapter 5 (Table 2) confirms.
claim_text: Sum of stage budgets ~2s to first token at ~p98 (union bound); composed run ingress-to-first-token p99 ~1.3s, confirmed by measured join in Chapter 5.

anchor: The specific bounds double Dynamo's default planner targets (500/50 ms, window-mean) applied as tail bounds, consistent with common practice in disaggregated-serving evaluations.
claim_text: Evaluation SLA bounds double Dynamo's default planner targets (500ms/50ms window-mean) as tail bounds.

anchor: Two windows are swept at the locked 2×2-worker topology: the steady 2,000-request head (2.77 req/s, 8.0 img/s) and the window enveloping the week's largest burst episode (Section 4.2, padded ±10 minutes: 64,804 requests over 8.3 hours, mean 2.17 req/s but 116 img/s, peaking at 370 img/s).
claim_text: Two sweep windows: steady 2000-request head (2.77 req/s, 8.0 img/s); burst window 64,804 requests over 8.3h (mean 2.17 req/s, 116 img/s, peak 370 img/s).

anchor: LLM / poly & steady & s=3 (ITL-bound) & 8.3 req/s & 248 → 374
claim_text: LLM polynomial steady: knee s=3 (ITL-bound), offered load 8.3 req/s, TTFT p99 248→374 ms.

anchor: LLM / AIC & steady & s=2 (ITL-bound) & 5.5 req/s & 307 → 418
claim_text: LLM AIC steady: knee s=2 (ITL-bound), offered load 5.5 req/s, TTFT p99 307→418 ms.

anchor: LLM / poly & burst & s=1 & 2.2 req/s & 910 at s=1
claim_text: LLM polynomial burst: knee s=1, offered load 2.2 req/s, TTFT p99 910 ms at s=1.

anchor: LLM / AIC & burst & none: over at s=1 & 2.2 req/s & 1,868 at s=1
claim_text: LLM AIC burst: no knee (over at s=1), offered load 2.2 req/s, TTFT p99 1868 ms at s=1.

anchor: Vision / AIC & steady & ≥ s=32 (cens.) & ≥ 256 img/s & 199 → 787
claim_text: Vision AIC steady: knee ≥ s=32 (censored), offered load ≥256 img/s, encoder delay p99 199→787 ms.

anchor: Vision / AIC & burst & none: over at s=1 & 116 img/s & 5,013 at s=1
claim_text: Vision AIC burst: no knee (over at s=1), offered load 116 img/s, encoder delay p99 5013 ms at s=1.

anchor: On the steady window (blue) the language knee sits at s=3 (polynomial) and s=2 (calibrated) while the vision pool remains under its bound through s=32; at the calibrated language knee the encoder idles at 4.5% utilization.
claim_text: Steady window: language knee s=3 (poly) and s=2 (AIC); vision pool under bound through s=32; at calibrated language knee encoder utilization 4.5%.

anchor: On the burst window (green) both calibrated curves start above their bounds at the episode's own recorded rate: the language pool at 1.9× its TTFT bound (the TP1 prefill floor; the polynomial model, 9% under the bound at the same point, misses this failure entirely), the vision pool at 5× its delay bound.
claim_text: Burst window: calibrated language pool at 1.9× TTFT bound (TP1 prefill floor), polynomial 9% under bound; vision pool at 5× delay bound.

anchor: No single load axis serves both pools.
claim_text: No single load axis can serve both pools due to different saturation characteristics.

anchor: On the steady head the separation is an order of magnitude: the vision pool is uncrossed at 32× the trace rate while the language knee sits at s=3 (polynomial) or s=2 (calibrated). Since the sweep is octave-spaced above s=4, the separation is a factor >10 under calibrated timing, so sizing both pools off one signal would overprovision the encoder fleet by that factor in calm traffic.
claim_text: Steady traffic saturation knees separated by >10× under calibrated timing (vision uncrossed at 32×, language knee at s=2); sizing off one signal overprovisions encoder fleet >10×.

anchor: At the knee's successor point the TTFT budget still has 1.8--2.1× slack while ITL p99 has crossed, so language-pool capacity under an interactive SLA is set by sustained token throughput per user.
claim_text: At language knee successor point, TTFT budget has 1.8-2.1× slack while ITL p99 crosses; capacity set by sustained token throughput per user.

anchor: Under the polynomial the pool skirts its bound at the episode's own rate (910 ms, 9% under). Under AIC timing the same run reads 1868 ms: the frames-class requests' ≈36k-token prefills alone exceed the TTFT budget at TP1, a prefill floor that persists at any worker count.
claim_text: Polynomial: 910 ms TTFT p99 (9% under bound); AIC: 1868 ms TTFT p99, frames-class ~36k-token prefills exceed TTFT budget at TP1, prefill floor persists at any worker count.

anchor: The baseline chapter's grid finds TTFT p99 pinned near 1.3 s from 4 through 16 TP1 workers on this window.
claim_text: Baseline grid: TTFT p99 ~1.3s from 4 to 16 TP1 workers on burst window.

anchor: TP2 at the same worker count (four GPUs in total) passes the window with 748 ms TTFT p99 and 6.6 ms ITL p99 --- the full SLA, with margin, at the episode's rate.
claim_text: TP2 (4 GPUs) passes burst window with 748 ms TTFT p99 and 6.6 ms ITL p99, meeting SLA with margin.

anchor: The vision pool's failure has no such fix: its p99 encoder delay of 5.0 s (5× the bound) arises from episodic queueing while mean utilization sits at 29%, is invisible to rate- and mean-utilization monitors (the minute-mean stays low even as the 1-minute peak busy fraction reaches 0.90), and yields only to capacity (the grid, AIC-costed: six encoder workers, 3× this topology, are needed at the trace's own rate).
claim_text: Vision pool burst failure: p99 encoder delay 5.0s (5× bound) from episodic queueing at 29% mean utilization, invisible to rate/util monitors (1-min peak busy fraction 0.90); needs 6 encoder workers (3× topology) at trace rate.

anchor: The window's 7,716 frames-class requests (>64 images each) decompose into chunk units of at most 64 images that, with smaller requests batched behind them, drive 83,376 forwards over the window; arrivals clump, the worst second landing 2,726 images at once.
claim_text: Burst window: 7,716 frames-class requests (>64 images) → 83,376 forwards; worst second 2,726 images.

anchor: Behind a strict FIFO, a frames flood monopolizes every worker at once: the backlog exceeds 1,000 queued images for 805 seconds across the eight-hour window, peaking at 4,701, each excursion a multi-second p99 event, yet the pool drains fully between excursions.
claim_text: FIFO queue: backlog >1000 queued images for 805s, peak 4701, each excursion multi-second p99 event, pool drains fully between excursions.

anchor: Under a lax TTFT-only 2 s bound the language knees sit one to two octaves higher.
claim_text: With lax TTFT-only 2s bound, language knees shift 1-2 octaves higher.

anchor: The polynomial-versus-AIC comparison quantifies the conclusions' sensitivity to that timing model, which is not the same as its accuracy; the steady-window knee moves by one sweep step between the two models and the burst verdict changes outright.
claim_text: Polynomial vs AIC: steady knee moves one sweep step, burst verdict changes entirely; shows sensitivity not accuracy.

anchor: The ≈3.1% of requests beyond the collected 16384-token grid (a share counted under the trace-token convention) are priced by extrapolation --- including the frames-class prefills that decide the burst-window TTFT tail.
claim_text: ~3.1% of requests exceed 16384-token grid, priced by extrapolation, including frames-class prefills determining burst TTFT tail.

anchor: The simulation costs encoder work as a full 448^2 forward per image and ships 196 × 4096 post-merge tokens per image across the seam, but sets the language pool's prefill length to the trace's ContextTokens verbatim --- which embeds the traced model's vision tokenization (≈66 tokens per image), roughly 3× below a Qwen3-VL-consistent 196-per-image prefill.
claim_text: Encoder cost: 448^2 forward per image, ships 196×4096 tokens/image; language prefill uses trace ContextTokens (~66 tokens/image) vs Qwen3-VL 196 tokens/image (3× difference).

anchor: Frames-class language work is thus undercounted (making the language pool look better in bursts) while the uniform 448^2 assumption overstates frames-class encoder work (making the vision pool look worse); both biases lean toward the burst asymmetry above.
claim_text: Token accounting biases: language work undercounted (better burst appearance), encoder work overstated (worse vision appearance), both lean toward burst asymmetry.

anchor: The TP1 prefill floor is robust to them (it worsens at 3× the tokens); the TP2 margin is not.
claim_text: TP1 prefill floor robust to token accounting biases (worsens at 3× tokens); TP2 margin not robust.

anchor: All encoder timing derives from a single RTX 5090 node (locked clocks); cross-unit silicon variance is unquantified.
claim_text: Encoder timing from single RTX 5090 node (locked clocks); cross-unit variance unquantified.

anchor: Repricing the encoder at other resolutions through the collected RTX 5090 operator database, the burst-window verdict holds at 448^2 and below on both modelled fabrics, with the service floor crossing the bound near 690--705 px, so the assumed resolution sits just below it.
claim_text: Burst verdict holds at 448^2 and below; service floor crosses bound near 690-705 px; assumed resolution just below crossing.

anchor: Provisioned worker-time is invariant across image size, because the schedule is driven by image count and is blind to size --- a size increase arrives as pure service-time inflation with no provisioning response.
claim_text: Provisioned worker-time invariant to image size; schedule driven by image count, size increase causes pure service-time inflation without provisioning response.

anchor: The 672^2 margin on the faster fabric is thin and reflects the single-stream handoff assumption, and on the sustained 24-hour window 672^2 misses the bound on both fabrics --- so that fabric margin is a burst-window result and must never be quoted without its window.
claim_text: 672^2 margin thin on faster fabric (single-stream handoff assumption); on 24h window 672^2 misses bound on both fabrics; margin is burst-window result only.

anchor: The dispatch cap is not the source of the burst verdict (verified across caps 32/64/128).
claim_text: Dispatch cap not source of burst verdict (verified across caps 32, 64, 128).

anchor: The handoff term remains the bandwidth-only, DeepStack-undercounting bound, not a measured NIXL curve.
claim_text: Handoff bound is bandwidth-only, undercounts DeepStack, not a measured NIXL curve.

anchor: Request ingress (image fetch/decode, preprocessing, tokenization, front-end queueing) is not simulated; the boundary is accelerator-side service and queueing.
claim_text: Request ingress (fetch, decode, preprocessing, tokenization, front-end queueing) not simulated; boundary is accelerator-side service and queueing.

anchor: Encoder delays fold into language-pool arrivals through the trace seam, which serializes the pools per request (no speculative overlap of encoder and prefill work); this is conservative for composed TTFT (overlap could only lower it).
claim_text: Trace seam serializes pools per request (no speculative encoder/prefill overlap); conservative for composed TTFT.

anchor: Per-pool knees were measured with the other pool absent (isolation trace / converter-only), making them attributable; composed-system claims are made only where composed runs exist (the baseline chapter's grid, which re-derives per-window optima across all six burst windows and a 24-hour steady window).
claim_text: Per-pool knees measured in isolation (other pool absent); composed claims only from composed runs (baseline grid across 6 burst windows + 24h steady).

anchor: The steady head used here is vision-lean (2.9 images per request against the trace's ≈14), which the 24-hour steady window corrects.
claim_text: Steady head vision-lean: 2.9 images/request vs trace ~14; 24h steady window corrects this.

anchor: On steady traffic the pools saturate an order of magnitude apart, and inside the largest burst both fail at the naive topology, differently --- a removable TP1 prefill floor against episodic FIFO queueing that yields only to capacity.
claim_text: Steady traffic: pools saturate order of magnitude apart; largest burst: both fail at naive topology differently (removable TP1 prefill floor vs episodic FIFO queueing needing capacity).

anchor: A single scaling signal cannot serve both pools, and the one the vision pool needs is invisible to the monitors reactive systems watch.
claim_text: Single scaling signal cannot serve both pools; vision pool's needed signal invisible to reactive system monitors.
